brief:
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, now leader of the Yashar party, challenged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's characterization of Iran as an imminent threat requiring immediate military strikes, Al-Monitor reported. Eisenkot argued the Iranian threat does not warrant urgent military action, contradicting Netanyahu's position that confronting Tehran is pressing.

The disagreement reflects a broader split within Israeli leadership over the appropriate response to Iran. Eisenkot's assessment carries particular weight given his background as former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces.
dek: Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot argues that the Iranian threat does not warrant an immediate military strike despite Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's insistence that confronting the threat is urgent.
title: Eisenkot disputes Netanyahu's urgency on Iran military action
